lines.text: Prince Darling turned to the Fairy and said, "I now understand the error of
my ways. I promise you, dear Fairy, that I will try to be kind and perform good
deeds in the future."
His voice was filled with determination, but unfortunately, he did not keep
his word.
Chapter 3 The Prince's Wrongdoing
Though Good King was the prince's
loving father, he wasn't the only person
who raised him. Prince Darling had
also been brought up by a foolish nurse,
who always spoiled him since he was a
child. When the prince wanted anything,
he only had to cry and stamp his feet
and she would give him whatever he asked for. This made him grow up to be
stubborn and selfish, not patient or generous like his father. The nurse, in her
foolish fondness, would often sit by Prince Darling's side and tell him, "Remember,
my dear, one day you will be King. As a king, you can do whatever you please.
No one will have the power to stop you." Her words, repeated day and night,
influenced the young prince deeply.
When the prince grew up, he learned that being proud was not good. Because
he saw his father's kindness, the prince tried to fix his bad habits. However, they
had become a part of his life, and a bad habit is very hard to get rid of.
Despite his anger or pride, he felt sorrow because he wasn't a bad man at
heart. "I'm very unhappy to have to struggle against my anger and pride every
